subject: math

unit.title: Place value to 100
unit.essentialQuestion: How do the tens and the ones decide how big a number is?

title: Comparing two-digit numbers
objectives: By the end, I can compare two two-digit numbers by looking at the tens first.

vocabulary.definition: decide which number is bigger or smaller
bigger than — the open mouth eats the bigger number
the golden rule: compare the tens digits before the ones

emphasize: COMPARE THE TENS FIRST. Only when the tens are equal do you look at the ones.
Pre-empt the big misconception '19 > 21 because 9 > 1' — the taller tens-tower wins.
The open mouth of > / < eats the bigger number.

misconceptions: '19 > 21 because 9 > 1' — comparing ones and ignoring tens
pointing the > / < mouth the wrong way
guessing without a strategy when numbers look close
hooks: Two houses on a street — 38 and 41. The postman walks from number 1 upwards: which house does he reach first?
priorKnowledge: partitioning — a digit's place gives its value (Lesson 2)

digital: side-by-side virtual rod towers on the whiteboard

video.title: Greater Than Less Than Song for Kids | Comparing Numbers to 1000
video.watchTask: Every time the mouth symbol appears, point which way it opens — toward the BIGGER number.

afterCheck.question: Which number does the open mouth always point to?

plan.goal: Pose the postman puzzle (38 vs 41); retrieve tens counting.
plan.note: Let the child predict before any teaching.
plan.successCriteria: Child states 3 tens for 38 and 4 tens for 41.

script.say: Two houses on a street: number 38 and number 41. The postman starts at house number 1 and walks up. Which house does he reach FIRST — which number is smaller? Take a guess! … Before we check: how many tens in 38? And in 41?
script.adaptHints: Swap postman for a delivery the child likes (pizza, parcels). Listen for '3 tens' and '4 tens'.

blocks.caption: Which house does the postman reach first?

stuckProtocol: If tens are shaky: draw both numbers as rods and count the rods in tens.

plan.goal: Model tens-first comparison with side-by-side rod towers; introduce > as the hungry mouth.
plan.note: The visual is the fix for '19 > 21': towers make the tens difference undeniable.
plan.successCriteria: Child hears and sees: more tens = bigger number, even when the ones look bigger.

script.say: I'll draw both numbers and stand their tens side by side, like towers. 41 has 4 tens — a taller tower. 38 has only 3 tens. More tens means a bigger number — so 41 is greater than 38, EVEN THOUGH 38 has more ones! I always look at the TENS FIRST. And look — I write it with the hungry mouth: 41 > 38. The mouth always opens to eat the bigger number!
script.adaptHints: Chomp sound for the mouth if the child enjoys it. Repeat the anchor: 'Tens first. The taller tower wins.'

elements.value: the mouth eats the bigger number

plan.goal: Shared example with EQUAL tens: 47 vs 43 — discover the fallback to ones.
plan.note: The child must articulate the next step themselves: 'tens are the same → check the ones.'
plan.successCriteria: Child says the tens are equal so we compare ones; concludes 47 > 43.

script.say: Now the tricky one — 47 and 43. I've drawn both towers… wait. Four tens and four tens. The towers are EXACTLY the same height! So what do we check now? … Yes — when the tens tie, the ONES break the tie. 7 beats 3, so 47 is greater. Write it with me: 47 > 43.
script.adaptHints: Give the child time to propose 'check the ones' before revealing.

blocks.prompt: The tens are EQUAL (4 and 4). What do we do next?
options: Pick the one that sounds bigger
blocks.explain: When tens tie, the ones break the tie: 7 > 3, so 47 > 43.

check.question: 47 vs 43 — which is greater and why?
check.expectedAnswer: 47, because the tens are equal so we compare ones: 7 > 3

wrongAnswers.remedy: The towers tie — but look at the loose cubes next to each tower. Who has more?
Count the ones on each side: 7 cubes vs 3 cubes.

plan.note: THE diagnostic of this lesson. '19, because 9 > 1' = ones-first misconception.
plan.successCriteria: Child picks 21 and justifies with tens ('2 tens beats 1 ten').

script.say: Trap question — ready? Which is bigger: 19 or 21? Think about the golden rule before you answer…
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'How did you decide?' Expect 'tens first'.

blocks.explain: Tens first! 2 tens (20) beats 1 ten (10). The big 9 can't save 19 — it's only 9 ones.

wrongAnswers.why: compared the ones and ignored the tens
wrongAnswers.remedy: Draw both towers. Whose tens-tower is taller — 1 ten or 2 tens?
Where do we ALWAYS look first? Point at the tens digits.

plan.goal: Independent comparing with > and <: far-apart tens, equal tens, and across-a-ten pairs.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Core set mirrors the script: 27 vs 72, 64 vs 61, 50 vs 49.
plan.successCriteria: Child compares 3+ pairs correctly with tens-first reasoning, including one equal-tens pair, recording with > or <.

script.say: Your turn, number detective! I'll show you pairs — you tell me who's bigger and write it with the hungry mouth. Remember the golden rule…
script.adaptHints: Frame pairs as scores/prices from the child's interests. Never change the numbers.

stuckProtocol: Go concrete: draw both tower pairs side by side.
One hint: 'Tens first — count the rods.'
Re-ask with very different tens (30 vs 80), then return.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise — smaller step.'

plan.goal: Child states the golden rule; end on a win.
plan.successCriteria: Child says: 'look at the tens first; if equal, look at the ones.'

script.say: Say the golden rule for comparing two numbers — teach it to me! … Perfect. You stopped yourself from being tricked by the ones and checked the tens — brilliant control.
script.adaptHints: Reference the specific trap they beat (19 vs 21 or their own near-miss).

wrongAnswers.remedy: Count each tower in tens: 10-20-30 vs 10-20-…-80. Which climb is longer?

hints: Count both in tens.
Which tower is taller — 3 rods or 8 rods?

reteach.say: Easy towers: 30 is three rods, 80 is eight rods. Eight rods tower over three. 80 > 30.

block.prompt: The hungry mouth! Which is right?
block.explain: 52 is bigger (5 tens beats 2 tens), and the mouth opens toward it.

wrongAnswers.remedy: The open side eats the BIGGER number. Which number is bigger here?
Tens first: 5 tens or 2 tens — which is more?

hints: First decide the bigger number (tens first).
Then open the mouth toward it.

reteach.say: Two steps, always in order: 1) tens first — 52 has 5 tens, it's bigger. 2) open the mouth at it: 52 > 25. The mouth is greedy — it only eats the big one!

block.title: Compare like a pro
steps: Look at the tens: 5 tens vs 2 tens

block.explain: Same digits, different places: 72 has 7 tens, 27 has only 2 tens.

wrongAnswers.why: read them as the same / guessed
wrongAnswers.remedy: Same digits but different homes! How many tens in each? Draw the towers.

hints: Tens first: 2 tens vs 7 tens.
Partition both if unsure.

reteach.say: 27 and 72 use the same digits, but the place gives the power. 72 puts the 7 in the tens seat — seventy! 27 only gives it the ones seat. 72 > 27.

block.explain: Tens tie (6 and 6) — the ones break the tie: 4 > 1.

wrongAnswers.remedy: The towers tie — now count the loose cubes: 4 vs 1.
Tens equal, so check ones: which is more, 4 or 1?

hints: Are the tens the same? Then move to the ones.
6 tens = 6 tens… so who breaks the tie?

reteach.say: When towers tie, the tiebreaker is the cubes. 64 and 61 both have six rods — but 64 has 4 cubes and 61 has just 1. 64 > 61.

block.title: The tie-breaker rule
steps: Ties go to the ones: 4 vs 1

block.explain: 5 tens beats 4 tens — even though 49 has nine ones and 50 has none!

wrongAnswers.remedy: Nine ones is a lot — but a whole extra TEN is more. Draw the towers: 5 rods vs 4 rods and 9 cubes.
Neighbours aren't equal — count on: 49, then one more is…?

hints: Tens first: 5 tens vs 4 tens.
49 + 1 = ? That tells you who's ahead.

reteach.say: 49 is nine cubes past forty, but 50 is a WHOLE tower more — five full rods. One step after 49 comes 50, so 50 is ahead. 50 > 49.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Which number is bigger? The mouth must open toward IT — 41 is on the right, so the mouth opens right: <.

hints: First: who's bigger, 38 or 41?
Open the mouth toward the bigger one.

reteach.say: 38 and 41 — tens first: 3 tens vs 4 tens, so 41 is bigger. The greedy mouth opens toward 41: 38 < 41. Read it: '38 is less than 41.'

block.definition: less than — the small closed point faces the smaller number, the open mouth faces the bigger

block.statement: 68 is greater than 71 because 8 is greater than 1.
block.explain: Tens first! 7 tens beats 6 tens, so 71 > 68. The big ones digit can't outvote the tens.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Draw the towers: 6 rods vs 7 rods. Can 8 little cubes beat a whole extra rod?

hints: Which digit is the boss — tens or ones?
A rod is worth ten cubes. Can 8 cubes beat a rod?

reteach.say: Here's the secret: one rod = TEN cubes. So an extra rod always beats a handful of extra cubes. 71 has the extra rod — 71 > 68, no matter how shiny that 8 looks.

block.caption: One rod beats any pile of loose cubes under ten

block.explain: Tens first: 61 has 6 tens; 59 and 58 have only 5.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Line up all three tens: 5, 6, 5. Who has the most tens?

hints: Compare all the tens digits first.
Only one number has 6 tens.

reteach.say: Three racers, same rule: tens first. 59 and 58 both have 5 tens; 61 has 6 tens — it leads before we even look at the ones. 61 is the greatest.

block.prompt: Is 60 > 59? By how much? Type the difference.

wrongAnswers.why: compared tens digits only (6 vs 5) and answered in tens
wrongAnswers.remedy: Count on from 59: how many steps to reach 60?
Say the counting sequence: …58, 59, then comes…?

hints: Count on from 59.
They're neighbours on the number line.

reteach.say: 60 IS greater than 59 — but only by a single step. 59, then 60. Greater doesn't always mean far apart — sometimes the winner leads by one!

practiceBank.skill: build a number to beat another

block.prompt: Type ANY number bigger than 55 — then be ready to prove it with tens-first!

wrongAnswers.remedy: Check with the rule: your number's tens vs 5 tens. Does yours win — or tie and win on ones?

hints: Anything with 6+ tens wins instantly.
With 5 tens you need MORE than 5 ones.

reteach.say: Two ways to beat 55: bring more tens (60, 70, 91…), or tie the tens and beat the ones (56, 57, 58, 59). Your proof is the golden rule itself.

block.title: Beating 55
steps: Fewer tens → can never win, even 49!

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct → next level; at level 3, interleave (symbols, traps, three-number compares).
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → reteach with side-by-side towers, then a level-1 far-apart-tens item.
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one equal-tens pair and one trap item (19-vs-21 family), recorded with > or < → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'comparing two-digit numbers'.
struggleProtocol: Name why ('the ones distracted us' / 'the mouth flipped').
Go concrete: draw both tower pairs side by side.
One hint: 'Tens first — count the rods.'
Re-ask with very different tens (30 vs 80), then build back.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise — smaller step.'
adaptivity.personalization: Frame pairs as game scores, race times, or collection counts from LearnerModel.interests. Keep the golden-rule language identical.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable comparison; praise the strategy: 'you checked the tens before the ones tricked you.'

differentiation.support: Always draw the rod-towers side by side so the taller tens-stack is obvious; say the rule aloud before answering.
differentiation.stretch: Fluent > / < use; 'Is 60 > 59? By how much?'; compare three numbers; 'make a number bigger than 55 and prove it.'

extension: Rod duel — the character builds a secret number, the child builds theirs, reveal together: the bigger tens-tower wins the round; best of five.
assessmentEvidence: Child compares 2–3 pairs correctly using tens-first reasoning, including a pair with equal tens, and records with > or <.
revisitLater: Compare-two starter before Lesson 4 (ordering builds on it); resurface the 19-vs-21 trap in the end-of-unit check.
